jobs.title: Director of Advancement Analytics and Insights
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Director of Advancement Analytics and Insights is a high-level strategist responsible for designing, deploying, and leading comprehensive business intelligence and analytics functions within University Advancement. This role serves as the primary architect of data-driven fundraising frameworks at San José State University, turning complex data into actionable insights, delivering dashboards, forecasting, and strategic analysis that guide leadership and teams across the division.

The Director oversees a comprehensive philanthropy analytics strategy to support fundraising performance, engagement metrics, and campaign success, and data-informed decision-making across the division. The incumbent acts as a critical bridge between data structure (Advancement IT), data collection (Gifts and Records Administration), and data application (Prospect Research and Management, Development, Alumni Engagement), successfully championing a culture of data literacy, evidence-informed engagement, and proactive analytics across University Advancement.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the multi-year roadmap for advancement analytics, aligning data initiatives with philanthropic and engagement pipelines, university campaigns, and divisional priorities and performance goals
Serve as the division’s lead business intelligence analyst, leveraging data-driven insights to inform decision-making, identify opportunities, and drive strategic initiatives across departments
Partners with teams on division-wide data operations, guiding divisional staff, partners, and vendors to ensure consistent, high-quality analytical standards in accordance with CASE, AASP, and industry best practices
Design, implement, and standardize key performance indicators (KPIs), performance dashboards, and accountability frameworks for University Advancement teams and leadership
Design, build, and continuously optimize a comprehensive institutional suite of interactive dashboards, reports, and data outputs that track philanthropic productivity, pipeline velocity, and fundraiser production
Oversee the delivery of automated and self-service analytics reports to front-line gift officers and academic leaders, ensuring visual and data consistency
Translate highly complex multivariate data sets and data science configurations into clear, narrative-driven business insights tailored for non-technical internal users and foundation boards
Develop, deploy, and validate advanced predictive algorithms and statistical models (e.g., donor propensity, major gift affinity, and lifetime value modeling) to uncover untapped donor capacity
Build data-driven revenue projection and multi-year forecasting models to determine target objectives and track pipeline gaps
Integrate external wealth screening and relationship mapping data directly into automated internal scoring models

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Ability to communicate with constituents in a professional and respectful manner
Working knowledge of, or the ability to develop proficiency in, the appropriate and ethical use of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), in higher education and administrative contexts
Ability to apply emerging technologies to support operational effectiveness, data-informed decision-making, and service delivery to students, faculty, and staff
Demonstrated ability to support continuous improvement and organizational learning through the responsible application of technology within assigned areas of responsibility
Deep knowledge of predictive modeling, data mining, multivariate regression, and fundraising forecasting techniques within a higher education environment
Mastery of visualization software (specifically Microsoft Power BI) and the ability to construct secure, scalable row-level security dashboard architectures
Comprehensive knowledge of relational database structures and workflows inside complex advancement CRMs (such as Salesforce, Blackbaud CRM/NXT, Affinaquest, or Ellucian)
Strong understanding of CASE Reporting Standards and AASP data metric models
Superior capability to synthesize complex data matrices into narrative presentations and clear policy recommendations for university leadership
Ability to apply emerging technologies to support operational effectiveness, data-informed decision-making, and service delivery to students, faculty, and staff
Demonstrated ability to support continuous improvement and organizational learning through the responsible application of technology within assigned areas of responsibility
Ability to evaluate potential applications, promote responsible, ethical, and equitable use, and ensure alignment with institutional policies, regulatory requirements, and strategic priorities
Demonstrated ability to manage multi-phase analytics projects independently under tight deadlines while successfully driving tool adoption among resistant users
Exceptional judgment regarding donor data privacy laws (FERPA, GDPR, CCPA) and an uncompromised commitment to professional ethics

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in Data Science, Business Intelligence, Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, or a related field
Five (5) years of progressively responsible professional experience in data analysis, business intelligence, or institutional analytics
Experience leading large-scale analytics initiatives or acting as a primary system analyst/strategist in a complex institutional or corporate environment

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree or higher in Data Science, Analytics, Business Administration (MBA), or an equivalent field
Seven (7) or more years of experience in higher education advancement services, prospect development analytics, or public university foundation data systems
Experience with fundraising principles and methods
Direct experience supporting multi-million fundraising initiatives using predictive fundraising pipelines
Experience with the California State University system, auxiliary organization models, and campus data compliance standards
Experience with SQL for data extraction, Python or R for statistical data modeling, and experience utilizing generative AI plugins for prompt engineering and rapid analytics

Classification: Administrator II

Anticipated Hiring Range: $9,167/month - $10,000/month

CSU Salary Range: $5,053/month - $16,221/month

The final hiring salary will be commensurate with experience.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff, President & COO
jobs.description:
About Handshake

Handshake was founded on a simple belief that everyone deserves a path to a great career, regardless of where they went to school or who they know. Today, we power 25 million job seekers, 1 million+ employers, and 1,600 educational institutions.

In 2025, we started Handshake AI and built the fastest-growing AI data business in history. We work directly with frontier AI lab researchers to create evaluations, publish benchmarks, and push the boundary of data. We've grown from $0 to ~$1B run rate and pay ~$60M to over 30K individuals every month.

Why Join Handshake Now

Shape how every career evolves in the AI economy, at global scale, with impact your friends, family and peers can see and feel
Partner hand-in-hand with world-class AI labs, Fortune 500 partners and the world's top educational institutions
Work together with engineers, scientists, operators, and more from Palantir, Meta, Scale AI, and former YC founders
Build a massive, fast-growing business with billions in revenue

The Role

You will be the execution partner to Jonathan Stull, Handshake's President & COO. He has built Handshake hand in hand with CEO Garrett Lord for the past decade, and he partners with Garrett and the board on strategy and execution across the company.

He directly leads the Handshake Network and its global growth, plus the Careers revenue lines: Learning, Recruiting, and International. The Handshake network is compounding fast (new user acquisition up 200%, WAU up 70%), and we're investing hard to accelerate that growth by opening new international markets and broadening the product suite to 10x our TAM, with two major acquisitions closed in the past two months.

Every major question about AI and work runs through this business, and you will sit inside every major decision and be expected to move it forward. This seat is a proven accelerator at Handshake: the people who have held roles like this have gone on to run functions as VPs and GMs. If you perform, your next role is a big one.

What You Will Own

The operating rhythm of the business: planning, staff meetings, operating reviews, and board prep. Decisions get made, owners get named, and threads never drop on your watch
First drafts before anyone asks. When a problem gets flagged on Monday, you show up with a proposed answer, and the answer reflects what your principal actually thinks and where his focus is
An independent, data-driven view of business performance. You interrogate the datasets, build the models, and say what the numbers show even when it is inconvenient
Communications that impact the company and the market: board materials, exec memos, and partner-facing narratives with zero filler
Strategic projects with no natural owner, carried end to end. Projects here hit resistance. You treat pushback as input to the next draft and keep moving
AI leverage across the business. Finding and installing AI workflows that make the whole team faster is a recurring part of the job, and you should be doing it to your own work first
Representing him in rooms he cannot be in, with judgment, discretion, and calm

How You Will Drive Success

This is not a 9 to 5 job. The pace is intense, context switches fast, and your principal will lean on you heavily.

You have been the right hand to a demanding senior leader and carried work end to end yourself. You can walk us through the artifacts
You are proactive to the point of impatience. You have never waited to be told what to do, and your former managers will say so. We will ask them
You can sit in a messy hour of debate and produce the one page that captures what your principal thinks, what was decided, and what happens next
You keep projects moving through pushback. Pausing at the first sign of resistance is the failure mode for this role
You are analytically self-sufficient: financial models, large datasets, SQL or the ability to pick it up fast
Your writing does not need editing
Low ego, high trust. You earn influence through judgment, clarity, and follow-through

Background That Predicts Success

5+ years where producing decision-ready work for senior leaders was the job itself: strategy consulting, banking or investing, corp dev, or strategy & ops in direct service of a C-level executive
Rapid progression in a high-bar environment that rewarded speed over process
AI fluency: you use AI daily to create leverage in your own work (formal AI experience not required)
Energized by Handshake's mission to expand access to opportunity in the AI economy

Bonus Points

Experience with marketplaces or multi-sided platforms
Exposure to board, financing, or public-market milestones
Familiarity with the AI data, evaluation, or annotation ecosystem

We Offer

Handshake delivers benefits that help you feel supported—and thrive at work and in life.

The below benefits are for full-time US employees.

🎯 Ownership:
Equity in a fast-growing company

💰 Financial Wellness:
401(k) match, competitive compensation, financial coaching

🍼 Family Support:
Paid parental leave, fertility benefits, parental coaching

💝 Wellbeing:
Medical, dental, and vision, mental health support, $500 wellness stipend

📚 Growth:
$2,000 learning stipend, ongoing development

💻 Remote & Office:
Internet, commuting, and free lunch/gym in our SF office

🏝 Time Off:
Flexible PTO, 15 holidays + 2 flex days

🤝 Connection:
Team outings & referral bonuses

Explore our mission, values, and comprehensive US benefits at joinhandshake.com/careers.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Vanderbilt University is seeking an exceptionally capable, politically astute, and operationally sophisticated leader to serve as Executive Director in the Office of the Chancellor
in Vanderbilt University, Nashville, TN.

This is a high-trust position at the center of one of the nation’s preeminent private research universities during a period of significant momentum, investment, and growth. The Executive Director will serve as a senior operational leader for the Chancellor’s Office—connecting information, people, priorities, and commitments across the institution so the Chancellor can operate at the highest possible level.

The person in this role will maintain a broad view of the Chancellor’s time, interactions, travel, preparation, and institutional responsibilities. You will work closely with the Chancellor, Chief of Staff, Vice Chancellors, senior university leaders, and a wide range of external stakeholders. You will identify what is missing, surface competing priorities, make informed judgment calls, and ensure the Chancellor’s intent is translated into coordinated action.

This role reports to the Chief of Staff and oversees two Senior Executive Coordinators and the Assistant Director of Briefings and Research. You will travel with the Chancellor as needed, particularly during high-stakes engagements and while learning the full rhythm, scope, and complexity of the role.

The Executive Director will exercise authority with discretion, make sound decisions, and operate effectively in an environment where pace, visibility, and expectations are high. The right person will reduce noise, improve coordination, protect the Chancellor’s time, and bring order to a demanding operation with many moving parts.

ABOUT VANDERBILT UNIVERSITY

Vanderbilt University is in Nashville, Tennessee, with more than 13,000 students and more than 7,000 faculty and staff. Vanderbilt University offers undergraduate programs in the liberal arts and sciences, engineering, music, education, and human development, as well as a full range of graduate and professional degrees in its 11 colleges and schools. Vanderbilt University spurs cross-disciplinary research to foster discoveries that impact society for the better. “Radical Collaboration,” in a culture where Vanderbilt community members can simultaneously challenge and support one another, is one of Vanderbilt’s most closely held values.

Vanderbilt is proud of what has been achieved in its first 153 years and is continuing to drive forward into bold new areas of growth. Vanderbilt is expanding its business and education programs to West Palm Beach, Florida; is establishing a full-time academic campus in San Francisco focused on innovative education and interdisciplinary collaboration that integrates technology, design, and the arts in a global center for innovation, entrepreneurship, and creativity; and has established a campus in New York City that serves as a hub for immersive learning, academic programming, and engagement with alumni and industry partners.

The Chancellor’s Office works across this entire enterprise. It coordinates closely with senior university leadership and the Board of Trust while supporting the Chancellor’s institutional, philanthropic, civic, political, academic, and public-facing responsibilities. He is a combination of a Chancellor, a CEO and a public figure, and his increasing visibility has created demands that require a more sophisticated executive-office structure.

Read more about Vanderbilt University HERE.
Read more about Chancellor Daniel Diermeier HERE.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

CHANCELLOR’S OFFICE LEADERSHIP

Lead the day-to-day administrative work for the Chancellor.
Directly oversee the Senior Executive Coordinator, Assistant Director of Briefings and Research, and other administrative support staff as assigned, ensuring the team functions as a collaborative, high-performing team that communicates openly, and shares context.
Establish clear roles, decision rights, escalation points, and communication protocols across the office.
Create the structure, rhythm, and accountability required to prevent missed information, duplicated work, dropped commitments, and unnecessary churn.
Absorb matters that require judgment and coordination without unnecessarily escalating every decision.

CALENDAR STRATEGY & EXECUTIVE TIME

Own the strategic framework governing how the Chancellor’s time is allocated.
Partner with the Chancellor, Chief of Staff, and Senior Executive Coordinator to evaluate meeting requests, institutional priorities, travel demands, media opportunities, and external engagements.
Determine what belongs on the Chancellor’s calendar, what should be delegated or declined, and where tradeoffs must be made.
Protect time for writing, strategic thinking, and focus, and strategically reduce inefficient travel.
Maintain a forward-looking view of the Chancellor’s commitments across the institution and beyond.

INSTITUTIONAL COORDINATION

Connect information and activity across executive leader offices and other university functions to build strong working relationships.
Ensure the Chancellor’s direction is understood, translated accurately, and carried forward
Coordinate complex engagements that involve multiple offices, stakeholders, and competing timelines, following up when information is incomplete or responsibilities are unclear.

BRIEFINGS, PREPARATION & INFORMATION FLOW

Set the strategic direction for the Chancellor’s briefing process in partnership with the Assistant Director of Briefings and Research.
Ensure the Chancellor receives the right level of information, context, analysis, and stakeholder intelligence before each significant interaction.
Create reliable systems to identify when information is missing, inconsistent, overly detailed, politically sensitive, or insufficient for the Chancellor to make an informed decision.

EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENTS & PROTOCOL

Serve as a point of contact for trustees, donors, elected officials, corporate executives, civic leaders, and media, representing the Chancellor with maturity, discretion, credibility, and sound judgment.
Coordinate high-level external engagements, including objectives, participants, protocol, preparation, logistics, and follow-up.

SYSTEMS, TECHNOLOGY & OPERATIONAL IMPROVEMENT

A seasoned executive-office leader with the judgment and presence to operate credibly with senior university leaders, trustees, donors, CEOs, elected officials, and other high-profile stakeholders.
A strategic operator who sees the whole board, connects information quickly, and understands the downstream impact of decisions.

Reporting to the Vice President of Advancement & Communications, the Executive Director is responsible for protecting and enhancing the College's reputation, strengthening stakeholder engagement, increasing institutional visibility, and supporting strategic enrollment, workforce development, student success, community engagement, and fundraising objectives through effective communications and storytelling.

Provides strategic leadership for all internal and external communications activities, ensuring consistency, accuracy, and alignment with institutional priorities.

About Handshake

Handshake was founded on a simple belief that everyone deserves a path to a great career, regardless of where they went to school or who they know. Today, we power 25 million job seekers, 1 million+ employers, and 1,600 educational institutions.

In 2025, we started Handshake AI and built the fastest-growing AI data business in history. We work directly with frontier AI lab researchers to create evaluations, publish benchmarks, and push the boundary of data. We've grown from $0 to ~$1B run rate and pay ~$60M to over 30K individuals every month.

Why Join Handshake Now

Shape how every career evolves in the AI economy, at global scale, with impact your friends, family and peers can see and feel
Partner hand-in-hand with world-class AI labs, Fortune 500 partners and the world's top educational institutions
Work together with engineers, scientists, operators, and more from Palantir, Meta, Scale AI, and former YC founders
Build a massive, fast-growing business with billions in revenue

The Role

You will be the execution partner to Jonathan Stull, Handshake's President & COO. He has built Handshake hand in hand with CEO Garrett Lord for the past decade, and he partners with Garrett and the board on strategy and execution across the company.

He directly leads the Handshake Network and its global growth, plus the Careers revenue lines: Learning, Recruiting, and International. The Handshake network is compounding fast (new user acquisition up 200%, WAU up 70%), and we're investing hard to accelerate that growth by opening new international markets and broadening the product suite to 10x our TAM, with two major acquisitions closed in the past two months.

Every major question about AI and work runs through this business, and you will sit inside every major decision and be expected to move it forward. This seat is a proven accelerator at Handshake: the people who have held roles like this have gone on to run functions as VPs and GMs. If you perform, your next role is a big one.

What You Will Own

The operating rhythm of the business: planning, staff meetings, operating reviews, and board prep. Decisions get made, owners get named, and threads never drop on your watch
First drafts before anyone asks. When a problem gets flagged on Monday, you show up with a proposed answer, and the answer reflects what your principal actually thinks and where his focus is
An independent, data-driven view of business performance. You interrogate the datasets, build the models, and say what the numbers show even when it is inconvenient
Communications that impact the company and the market: board materials, exec memos, and partner-facing narratives with zero filler
Strategic projects with no natural owner, carried end to end. Projects here hit resistance. You treat pushback as input to the next draft and keep moving
AI leverage across the business. Finding and installing AI workflows that make the whole team faster is a recurring part of the job, and you should be doing it to your own work first
Representing him in rooms he cannot be in, with judgment, discretion, and calm

How You Will Drive Success

This is not a 9 to 5 job. The pace is intense, context switches fast, and your principal will lean on you heavily.

You have been the right hand to a demanding senior leader and carried work end to end yourself. You can walk us through the artifacts
You are proactive to the point of impatience. You have never waited to be told what to do, and your former managers will say so. We will ask them
You can sit in a messy hour of debate and produce the one page that captures what your principal thinks, what was decided, and what happens next
You keep projects moving through pushback. Pausing at the first sign of resistance is the failure mode for this role
You are analytically self-sufficient: financial models, large datasets, SQL or the ability to pick it up fast
Your writing does not need editing
Low ego, high trust. You earn influence through judgment, clarity, and follow-through

Background That Predicts Success

5+ years where producing decision-ready work for senior leaders was the job itself: strategy consulting, banking or investing, corp dev, or strategy & ops in direct service of a C-level executive
Rapid progression in a high-bar environment that rewarded speed over process
AI fluency: you use AI daily to create leverage in your own work (formal AI experience not required)
Energized by Handshake's mission to expand access to opportunity in the AI economy

Bonus Points

Experience with marketplaces or multi-sided platforms
Exposure to board, financing, or public-market milestones
Familiarity with the AI data, evaluation, or annotation ecosystem

Handshake delivers benefits that help you feel supported—and thrive at work and in life.

Equity in a fast-growing company

401(k) match, competitive compensation, financial coaching

ABOUT THE ROLE

Vanderbilt University is seeking an exceptionally capable, politically astute, and operationally sophisticated leader to serve as Executive Director in the Office of the Chancellor

The person in this role will maintain a broad view of the Chancellor’s time, interactions, travel, preparation, and institutional responsibilities. You will work closely with the Chancellor, Chief of Staff, Vice Chancellors, senior university leaders, and a wide range of external stakeholders. You will identify what is missing, surface competing priorities, make informed judgment calls, and ensure the Chancellor’s intent is translated into coordinated action.

This role reports to the Chief of Staff and oversees two Senior Executive Coordinators and the Assistant Director of Briefings and Research. You will travel with the Chancellor as needed, particularly during high-stakes engagements and while learning the full rhythm, scope, and complexity of the role.

The Executive Director will exercise authority with discretion, make sound decisions, and operate effectively in an environment where pace, visibility, and expectations are high. The right person will reduce noise, improve coordination, protect the Chancellor’s time, and bring order to a demanding operation with many moving parts.

ABOUT VANDERBILT UNIVERSITY

Vanderbilt University is in Nashville, Tennessee, with more than 13,000 students and more than 7,000 faculty and staff. Vanderbilt University offers undergraduate programs in the liberal arts and sciences, engineering, music, education, and human development, as well as a full range of graduate and professional degrees in its 11 colleges and schools. Vanderbilt University spurs cross-disciplinary research to foster discoveries that impact society for the better. “Radical Collaboration,” in a culture where Vanderbilt community members can simultaneously challenge and support one another, is one of Vanderbilt’s most closely held values.

Vanderbilt is proud of what has been achieved in its first 153 years and is continuing to drive forward into bold new areas of growth. Vanderbilt is expanding its business and education programs to West Palm Beach, Florida; is establishing a full-time academic campus in San Francisco focused on innovative education and interdisciplinary collaboration that integrates technology, design, and the arts in a global center for innovation, entrepreneurship, and creativity; and has established a campus in New York City that serves as a hub for immersive learning, academic programming, and engagement with alumni and industry partners.

The Chancellor’s Office works across this entire enterprise. It coordinates closely with senior university leadership and the Board of Trust while supporting the Chancellor’s institutional, philanthropic, civic, political, academic, and public-facing responsibilities. He is a combination of a Chancellor, a CEO and a public figure, and his increasing visibility has created demands that require a more sophisticated executive-office structure.

Read more about Vanderbilt University HERE.
Read more about Chancellor Daniel Diermeier HERE.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

CHANCELLOR’S OFFICE LEADERSHIP

Lead the day-to-day administrative work for the Chancellor.
Directly oversee the Senior Executive Coordinator, Assistant Director of Briefings and Research, and other administrative support staff as assigned, ensuring the team functions as a collaborative, high-performing team that communicates openly, and shares context.
Establish clear roles, decision rights, escalation points, and communication protocols across the office.
Create the structure, rhythm, and accountability required to prevent missed information, duplicated work, dropped commitments, and unnecessary churn.
Absorb matters that require judgment and coordination without unnecessarily escalating every decision.

CALENDAR STRATEGY & EXECUTIVE TIME

Own the strategic framework governing how the Chancellor’s time is allocated.
Partner with the Chancellor, Chief of Staff, and Senior Executive Coordinator to evaluate meeting requests, institutional priorities, travel demands, media opportunities, and external engagements.
Determine what belongs on the Chancellor’s calendar, what should be delegated or declined, and where tradeoffs must be made.
Protect time for writing, strategic thinking, and focus, and strategically reduce inefficient travel.
Maintain a forward-looking view of the Chancellor’s commitments across the institution and beyond.

INSTITUTIONAL COORDINATION

Connect information and activity across executive leader offices and other university functions to build strong working relationships.
Ensure the Chancellor’s direction is understood, translated accurately, and carried forward
Coordinate complex engagements that involve multiple offices, stakeholders, and competing timelines, following up when information is incomplete or responsibilities are unclear.

BRIEFINGS, PREPARATION & INFORMATION FLOW

Set the strategic direction for the Chancellor’s briefing process in partnership with the Assistant Director of Briefings and Research.
Ensure the Chancellor receives the right level of information, context, analysis, and stakeholder intelligence before each significant interaction.
Create reliable systems to identify when information is missing, inconsistent, overly detailed, politically sensitive, or insufficient for the Chancellor to make an informed decision.

EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENTS & PROTOCOL

Serve as a point of contact for trustees, donors, elected officials, corporate executives, civic leaders, and media, representing the Chancellor with maturity, discretion, credibility, and sound judgment.
Coordinate high-level external engagements, including objectives, participants, protocol, preparation, logistics, and follow-up.
Travel with the Chancellor as needed for major university, donor, government, media, and stakeholder engagements.

SYSTEMS, TECHNOLOGY & OPERATIONAL IMPROVEMENT

Improve workflows related to calendar decisions, briefing preparation, information sharing, stakeholder management, and commitment tracking.
Lead the thoughtful use of AI to improve visibility and decision-making.
Use data to identify patterns in the Chancellor’s time, travel, and meeting load, then translate those findings into practical recommendations.
Provide the Chancellor with useful outputs and recommendations without expecting him to personally operate every tool.

WHO WILL SUCCEED IN THIS ROLE:

A seasoned executive-office leader with the judgment and presence to operate credibly with senior university leaders, trustees, donors, CEOs, elected officials, and other high-profile stakeholders.
A strategic operator who sees the whole board, connects information quickly, and understands the downstream impact of decisions.
Politically astute, institutionally aware, and highly discreet with sensitive information.
Comfortable exercising authority, making sound decisions, and communicating them without creating unnecessary friction or frequent intervention.
Intellectually confident and well prepared; able to challenge a powerful leader with facts, sound reasoning, and appropriate timing.
Calm under pressure and steady when priorities shift, stakes rise, information isn’t perfect or ideas are challenged. Thrives in unpredictability and scale while still close loops and holding priorities.
Operationally rigorous, with a strong instinct for systems, accountability, and follow-through.
Collaborative and low ego; able to lead a strong team while respecting the expertise and responsibilities of others. Enjoys consistent feedback.
Able to see around corners, resolve issues, and keep the Chancellor and the team appropriately informed without creating more noise.
Technologically curious and confident using AI, CRM systems, executive-office platforms, and data to improve decision-making.
Comfortable representing Vanderbilt’s values, including institutional neutrality, open inquiry, and civil discourse.

COMPENSATION, REQUIREMENTS & LOGISTICS
Full-time, benefits-eligible position based on Vanderbilt University’s campus in Nashville, Tennessee.
Travel with the Chancellor may be required, including domestic and occasional international travel.
A bachelor’s degree in management, public administration, communications, higher education, or a related field is required. An advanced degree is preferred.
